correctness.rationale: For the graph on 2n vertices with edges i↔i±1 and i↔i+n, an Ind_2 face is exactly a vertex subset inducing max degree≤1 (equivalently every component size≤2). Independently enumerated every nonempty bitmask and checked the supplied pivot orders, matched face pairs and topological acyclicity across all nonempty Hasse covers for n=4,5,6,7,8. Found respectively 78,232,685,2046,6078 faces; 38,111,339,1022,3023 Morse pairs; 192,720,2556,8946,30384 Hasse edges; one critical 0-cell plus k d-cells at (d,k)=(2,1),(3,9),(3,6),(4,1),(5,31). Entire Hasse digraph acyclic in all five. These finite exhaustive matchings and the CW theorem establish the *integral homotopy* wedges, not merely mod-p Betti ranks.

evidence: Total three-cut source gives BI_3(M2n) ≃ wedge^{1+C(n+1,2)} S^3 for all n≥5, where BI3 controls independent triples, not connected component sizes.
Agarwal–Basak classify Ind(M2n) and perfect matching but not Ind_2.
Sawant theorem hypotheses require a tree; Möbius ladders contain cycles.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broad published theorem on same graph actually covers a different functor, with explicit conflicting wedge ranks (n=5 BI3 has 16 S3 versus Ind_2 has 9 S3). No implication.

value.rationale: The five smallest nondegenerate cases immediately after M6=K3,3 show nontrivial changes of sphere dimension and multiplicity upon permitting induced isolated edges. The integral types form a motivated baseline for higher-independence topology on a natural symmetric cyclic graph family; no infinite-family classification is claimed or needed for this exact useful finite invariant.

limitations: An unindexed higher-Ind2 small-graph benchmark might have these counts under different nomenclature.
Different alternative higher-independence definitions should not be conflated with this component-size predicate.
